subject: Supplier onboarding: PO intake, billing cadence, and quick-pay option
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Supplier onboarding: PO intake, billing cadence, and quick-pay option

Hi Asha —

Welcome aboard, and thanks for moving quickly on the paperwork. To finish vendor activation and route POs to your AR team, we need the completed vendor intake form (attached) and a current W-9. Once those are in our vendor master, procurement will issue the first PO and our AP team will map your invoice lane.

A couple of items to align on up front so we don’t have surprises when your first invoice hits:
- Standard payment window we use for new suppliers is Net 45.
- We offer an optional QuickPay program (merchant-facing enrollment) that enables faster remittance in exchange for a small discount: 1.5% if paid within 10 calendar days. Enrollment is optional per supplier.
- If your AR prefers a different cadence (Net 30 or Net 60), please confirm — provide the preferred term and whether you want to opt into QuickPay.

For setup: please return the filled VendorOnboardingForm.xlsx and the W9. I’ve attached our MSA for reference (signed on both sides) and a simple invoice routing template so we can validate delivery addresses and remit contacts.

Next steps from our side after we receive forms:
1) Procurement issues PO and confirms PO number format.
2) AP validates invoice lane and QuickPay enrollment if applicable.
3) First PO sent and vendor activated.

If you can reply with form + W-9 by EOD tomorrow we’ll aim to have the PO issued within 3 business days.

Thanks —
David
David Kim
Head of Procurement Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: VendorOnboardingForm.xlsx, QubitWorks_W9.pdf, Signed_MSA.pdf

Hi David —

Thanks for the clear rundown and the warm welcome. Attaching the completed onboarding form and the W-9. Quick answers to your questions below and a note about our preferred terms:

- Preferred payment term: Net 60 is our standard for enterprise customers. That said, we’re open to contracting Net 45 to help with cashflow during the ramp.
- QuickPay: We can participate in a QuickPay program, but our standard discount for expedited settlement is 1% within 10 days (we typically see 1%–2% market range).
- For the first two invoices, we’d appreciate a one-time expedite to Net 30 while we finalize billing integrations.

We’ll need the PO number on the invoice and the exact remit-to address to ensure the AR team processes it correctly — I filled the invoice routing template with our preferred contact and AP email (ap@qubitworks.com).

Attached: VendorOnboardingForm.xlsx (completed), QubitWorks_W9.pdf, Signed_MSA.pdf

Let me know if the Net 60 -> Net 45 compromise is workable or if you’d prefer to lock Net 45 from the start.

Best,
Asha Ramesh
Head of Revenue Operations
QubitWorks
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-08T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Supplier onboarding: PO intake, billing cadence, and quick-pay option

David / Grace — forwarding Asha’s response and attachments. Summary + recommended options for finance approval:

Summary from vendor:
- Default asks for Net 60, willing to take Net 45.
- Requests one-time Net 30 for first two invoices while integrations complete.
- Willing to join QuickPay at 1% for 10-day settlement (vendor suggested).

Recommended response options (pick one):
1) Standard onboarding: accept Net 45 permanently. Offer QuickPay enrollment at 1.5%/10 days (Redwood subsidizes middle ground).
2) Compromise: accept Net 60 as contract baseline but grant a temporary Net 30 for first two invoices (to be clearly documented) and allow QuickPay at 1% permanent option.
3) Strict terms: require Net 45 with no temporary accelerations; allow QuickPay at 1.5% only.

Operational notes:
- Option 1 is easiest for our operational cadence (POs map to standard Net 45 lanes).
- Option 2 requires a short-lived exception ticket to AP to change the invoice lane for the first two invoices, then revert to Net 60 baseline — additional operational overhead.

As procurement lead, I recommend Option 1 (Net 45 baseline + QuickPay 1.5%/10d). It gets the vendor activated quickly, preserves a consistent lane for PO issuance, and gives them an incentive for faster payment.

Grace — can you confirm if Finance is comfortable with the 1.5% QuickPay rate? If you prefer the vendor-proposed 1% we should capture that as a permanent term.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Vendor Enablement Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Supplier onboarding: PO intake, billing cadence, and quick-pay option

Hi all —

Thanks for the clear options. Finance has reviewed and approves the following onboarding terms for QubitWorks:

- Baseline payment term: Net 45 (standard Redwood lane).
- Optional QuickPay enrollment: 1.5% discount for payment within 10 calendar days. Enrollment is elective; vendor to confirm intent.
- Temporary exception: we will accommodate a one-time Net 30 for the first two invoices while billing integrations finalize. This will be logged as a procurement exception and will automatically revert to Net 45 thereafter.

Operational steps we will take now:
1) Procurement (David) will issue the first PO with Net 45 terms and include a note: "One-time Net 30 for invoices 1–2 per exception ticket #AP-4521".
2) AP will enroll QubitWorks into the QuickPay program pending vendor confirmation.
3) Vendor to send invoices to ap@redwood-invoices.com with PO number visible on each invoice.

Asha — if you can confirm you accept Net 45 + the QuickPay option (and whether you want to enroll at 1.5% now or request the 1% rate), we will finalize the PO and complete activation.

Thanks — looking forward to working together.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
